chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Clarinet lessons he disliked
summary: His mother chose clarinet and a Japanese teacher; he hated it at about ten and was drawn to strings.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Back to Montgomery, I recall reading that you played clarinet before guitar, (Inaudible).
Yeah, and I hated it. I didn't -- I never --
Why did you start on clarinet? (Inaudible).

Well, I don't know, I didn't choose the clarinet. My mother chose the clarinet before me. And she got this Japanese teacher for me, and I don't think we could communicate too well. This is another reason I think I didn't like the instrument. And I always was drawn to strings, you know, so --
How old were you when you played clarinet?

Oh, about 10, around that. Yeah. No longer than I had to, you know. I never really got into it -- I never was a very good clarinet player because as I say I didn't like it. So it was the old story where they had to make me practice, but once I got to the strings they couldn't stop me from practicing. That was it.
